title: Foundational skills map & mentorship 9-day activation sprint
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational playbook for a 9-day "foundational skills + mentorship" activation sprint for new hires in engineering, product, and platform roles. The goal is a minimal, measurable ramp that combines a prioritized skills map, a lightweight interview rubric for final-stage screening, and a day-zero through day-9 onboarding/mentor cadence.

Context / why this exists (notes to self):
- Hiring velocity is good but onboarding feedback shows inconsistent early impact signals (first 2 weeks).
- Hypothesis: a focused, short activation sprint with explicit skills mapping + mentor micro-sprints will reduce time-to-first-meaningful-PR and surface early support needs.
- This doc is intentionally narrow (foundational skills only) — not a full 30/60/90. Keep it lightweight and iterative.

Sprint goals (metrics):
- Day 9: new hire submits at least 1 non-trivial PR (docs + code/test) or equivalent deliverable.
- Mentor and hiring manager give a 1-5 confidence score >= 3 on "foundational readiness" on day 9.
- Reduce "needs help" support tickets from new hires in week 1 by 30% vs cohort baseline.

High-level timeline (9 days):
- Day 0 (preboarding): access + baseline survey + repo clone checklist.
- Day 1: orientation intro, team context, defined first-PR task assigned (tiny but meaningful).
- Day 2-3: reading + pair sessions with mentor; first small implementation checkpoint.
- Day 4-6: independent work with daily 30m mentor syncs; focus on tests and CI.
- Day 7: PR ready for internal review (draft).
- Day 8: reviews/actions; finish documentation.
- Day 9: PR merged or explicit follow-up plan; 1:1 reflection + confidence survey.

Foundational skills map (prioritized for the sprint) - for sw/product/platform new hires:
- Repo literacy: clone, run tests locally, submit a branch-based PR. (critical)
- Basic observability: know where traces/errors surface for their service, read token-level traces in Console. (high)
- Local dev loop: build/test/debug cycle within 10-15m for small change. (high)
- Security & compliance basics: secret handling, KMS basics, SSO sign-in flow. (medium)
- Infra awareness: which infra tier (hosted, dedicated, private) the service lives on; basic deploy flow. (medium)
- Product context: customer impact of the area; 1-pager read + 5 min pitch. (low for sprint, but scheduled)

Interview rubric (compact, final-stage screening focus) - quick matrix to evaluate alignment with sprint outcomes:
- Repo literacy (score 1-5): Can candidate walk through a simple Git flow, explain PR review tradeoffs, and resolve a basic rebase conflict?
- Debug reasoning (1-5): Given a short trace/stack snippet, can candidate hypothesize likely root causes and next steps?
- Communication (1-5): Can they write a concise PR description and describe testing strategy?
- Learning velocity (1-5): Evidence of quickly picking up unfamiliar code or tech in prior roles; ask for a 30-60s story.
- Mentorship fit (1-3): Coachability and receptiveness — will they respond well to mentor-led micro-sprints?
Scoring guidance: target >= 12/20 for moving to offer for individual contributor IC2/IC3 roles. For senior IC, require 14+.

Day-zero checklist (preboarding) - must be automated where possible:
- Account creation: SSO invite sent, MFA enforced.
- Hardware: laptop assigned + standard image + 1 required app list.
- Seat access: repo, CI, Console, Observability dashboards (team-specific).
- First-PR stub: a tiny starter issue assigned in their repo ("fix lint in example test") with label "9-day-sprint".
- Baseline survey: 5 quick q's (comfort with git, testing, Linux, CI, observability).
- Mentor assigned and 1st sync scheduled (30m on Day 1).

Mentor pairing & cadence (recommended):
- Mentor = adjacent senior IC (not direct manager). Time commitment: ~3-4 hours total over 9 days.
- Suggested micro-sessions: Day1 30m onboarding; Day2 60m pair coding; Days 3-6 20-30m daily async syncs; Day8 30m PR review touch; Day9 30m reflection.
- Mentor checklist: help unblock, review tests, ensure CI passes, encourage small PRs, model good PR descriptions.

Onboarding artifacts / templates (short snippets to copy into welcome thread):
- PR template blurb: "What I changed, why, how to test locally, links to customer-impact doc"
- Pairing schedule template: Day2 10:30-12:00 pair; Day3 11:00 check-in; etc.
- Mini-retro template for Day9: "What helped most, what blocked me, 1 thing to improve in onboarding"

Risk log (quick):
- Risk: mentor bandwidth conflicts -> Mitigation: backup mentor + manager nudges; escalate via HR if > 48h stall.
- Risk: starter task too big -> Mitigation: break into sub-tasks, require an initial design note before coding.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Should the starter task be same across backend/frontend or tailored? (Pro: consistency; Con: mismatch to real work) -> ACTION: ask eng leads (ticket HR-419).
- Q: how to instrument metric for "support ticket reduction" reliably? need SRE and onboarding analytics input.
- TODO: draft automated baseline survey in Typeform + hook into onboarding Slack channel. Assigned: Maya.

Quick templates (copy/paste) - Mentor intro Slack message:
"Hey <name> — I'm <mentor>. My slack is @mentor. Plan: Day1 intro, Day2 pair, small daily syncs. Goal is to help you get a small PR merged by day 9. Ping me if blocked. Also here's a curated 30-min reading list: repo README -> dev-playbook -> first-PR-issue."

Acceptance & next steps:
- Iterate this sprint with first 6 new hires in Q1 2026 as a beta; collect mentor and new hire confidence scores; update sprint after 2 cohorts.
- Responsible: People Ops (Avery) + Eng leads (Diego).

Notes (informal):
- Keep things intentionally short. Avoid overloading new hires with too many meetings in week 1. Micro-sessions + async notes win.
- This should slot into existing "first-30" material — not replace it.

Linked references: Confluence mentorship framework (see link above), HR ticket HR-412 (mentorship pilot), onboarding analytics doc (TBD).

Last updated: 2025-11-15 by Avery Chen (draft).
